video: Tokenization: why the model never reads your words
note: Arc 1 Episode 1. One continuous 59.5s shot. Status is the only field a steady-state session flips. Never reword or delete acceptance criteria to make something pass - that is a correctness bug, not a shortcut.

features.title: Every id on screen is a verified tiktoken output, in one block
acceptance: ENCODING, VOCAB_SIZE, QUESTION, WORD, SENTENCE_TOKENS, SENTENCE_IDS, WORD_TOKENS, WORD_IDS live in one module-level block and every beat imports them
TokenStrip is never allowed to invent an id with fake_token_id - token_ids is passed explicitly
The vocabulary counter is rounded from VOCAB_SIZE in code, not typed
The four illustrative figures each carry the word on screen or are named as ours
Provenance of the encoding files, and how the mirror was authenticated, is recorded in script.md

features.title: The set: a bench read left to right, with one consequence spur
acceptance: Five bays on the bench line plus the wall above the table and the meter below it
Every travel path is built from the drawn rails via routing.join, never from bay centres
validate() asserts the bench run and the spur clear what they must, at construction
The pull-back width is derived and asserted against SHOT_WIDE within 12%
The shrink factor that puts the bench inside the ghost node is derived from the node, not typed

features.title: CharacterRow, MergeTable, VocabWall, GhostCircuit as local one-offs
acceptance: None of the four is promoted into /lib - they move only when a second scene needs one, with a test
CharacterRow derives its cells from the question string and counts its own r cells, scoped to a word
MergeTable finds each merge pair by what its cells currently spell, so no index is written down
GhostCircuit is ten faint nodes and one label, and does not import chatgpt_request_lifecycle
The module is NOT named props.py - that name is already taken on the flat scene path

features.title: 0.0-11.5s: the wrong answer, the character row, and the wipe
acceptance: The cold open holds still long enough for the wrong answer to feel wrong
The question leaves the bubble along the drawn rail, not a line between centres
Exactly the three r cells inside strawberry pulse; the standalone r in r's does not
The counter is labelled r in "strawberry" - 3, never a bare 3
At the end of the wipe all 27 cells are dark and the counter has gone with them

features.title: 11.5-21.0s: seven chips, the leading space, the strawberry punchline
acceptance: SEVEN chips, not the brief's nine, and ' strawberry' is one of them
The leading space is shown once, on an enlarged chip, with a caption saying what it means
The bare word's three pieces and the single sentence chip are on screen together
The row is whole again and both captions are gone by 21.0s
Every arrival is a FadeIn - nothing comes in on .animate.set_opacity

features.title: 21.0-33.5s: the vocabulary wall, three worked merges, the ramp
acceptance: The wall reads as texture with one readable counter beside it
Three merges each highlight their pair, close it up, and write onto the ordered list
The merge example is captioned as ours, not as the BPE paper's
The ramp accelerates out of legibility and is ONE click in the deck
merge 50,000 carries the word illustrative

features.title: 33.5-40.0s: seven integers through the model wall
acceptance: The integer faces are built from the strip's own token_ids - there is no second list
5299 1991 428 885 306 101830 30, and every digit matches the pre-flight
The row travels a routing.join path built from the drawn rail, through the slot
Past the wall there is no text anywhere, only vectors
The struck-through word and the integer that actually crossed are shown together

features.title: 40.0-51.0s: price, context, latency, and three languages
acceptance: The Burmese bar overruns the frame edge and is allowed to leave the shot
The median/MASSIVE/cl100k_base caption is on screen and above MIN_READABLE at SHOT_METER
The price row shows the unit and no figures
The context bar says illustrative on screen
The station header does not collide with the counters

features.title: 51.0-59.5s: the whole bench, then one bay of the Arc 0 plant
acceptance: Every bay and the bottom of the meter are inside the wide frame
Bay marquees are readable and nothing is clipped at the frame edge
The SET scales into the ghost node - the camera does not move
The shrunken bench is INSIDE the TOKENIZER node, not merely near it
The film ends on a trailing hold, so the deck's last stop rests past the final fade

features.title: The click-advanced deck
acceptance: Subclasses the film and defines no construct of its own
47 animations -> 40 stops, one suppressed region
The ramp is recognised by the mobject it animates, never by a play index
No stop is a single frame at the Evaluator's render profile

features.title: Lock timing against a recorded voice-over
acceptance: Narration is recorded and its per-beat timings measured
run_time values move to land beats on the narration, not the other way round
Total runtime stays under the 60.0s cap at the final profile

features.title: Check whether the bare ' r' chip misreads as a piece of strawberry
features.note: The sentence's ' r' token (428) renders as a bare 'r' chip two places from the strawberry chip, because display_token trims the leading space. The film's claim is scoped correctly and the counter is labelled, but a first-time viewer has not been tested on it. Worth a second pair of eyes before this ships publicly; the cheap fix if it does misread is show_space=True on the whole B2 row.
acceptance: Someone who has not read the script watches B1-B2 and is asked what the 'r' chip is
If it misreads, the row is redrawn with show_space=True and the frames re-reviewed
